parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the need for pure ESM .mjs modules in /output, exact CLI and bytes-output parity, from-scratch AES ECB, and no node:crypto or npm dependencies.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It used a first local executable probe, then assigned AES core to one child, pybytes plus args helpers to a second child, and the entry/integration/test task to a third child after the first two returned.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote /output/lib/aes.mjs, /output/lib/pybytes.mjs, /output/lib/args.mjs, and /output/test16.mjs. The final implementation used TextEncoder, split data into 16-byte blocks, encrypted with the helper, and printed CPython-style bytes repr.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The third child consumed the prior module contracts and wrote the entry file; the parent later read the helper modules and final-presented a compact /output/lib based structure plus test16.mjs.
parallel.verification: The children ran FIPS vectors, CPython bytes-repr checks, parser basics, four sample diffs, a missing --data comparison, and one extra random valid case, but the parent did not run an independent final whole-task evaluator before closing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed with 3/33. The trajectory also shows a lossy AES sample-vector handoff and a helper brief that narrowed the exact argparse parity requirement.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same pure ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, no node:crypto, exact CLI, AES ECB, block splitting, and bytes repr obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept all ownership in one main agent, implementing the AES modules, bytes repr, parser, entry file, and verification loop without subagents or handoff boundaries.
serial.implementation: It wrote a multi-file AES hierarchy under /output/aes, plus /output/pybytes.mjs, /output/args.mjs, and /output/test16.mjs, then later rewrote args.mjs for closer argparse behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because implementation was local, integration consisted of its own imports and rewrites rather than joining child outputs; final artifacts were collected successfully.
serial.verification: It diffed four sample cases, explored parser help/unknown/repeated/dash-value behavior, reran a larger suite with sample cases and fuzzing, and reported one remaining non-strict traceback text mismatch on invalid block length.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation also failed with 3/33. The raw trajectory does not expose the hidden evaluator mismatches, so the exact residual implementation defect cannot be isolated beyond observed local coverage limits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel captured the ESM, .mjs, no external dependency, no node:crypto, AES-ECB, block splitting, bytes repr, and CLI requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial captured the same requirements and later explored additional argparse parity details beyond the prompt examples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel delegated a narrower helper requirement to a child, while serial carried the exact CLI parity obligation through later local probing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assigned AES core and helper parsing/formatting to separate children, then assigned entry-file integration to a third child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained a single owner for AES, args, pybytes, entry, testing, and parser rewrites.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel split created child-brief and handoff boundaries; the serial path avoided those boundaries but did all work sequentially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave explicit function contracts for AES, pybytes, and args, but the helper brief narrowed exact argparse parity and the AES vector was transferred as a wrong hex value.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept the executable observations and parser behavior exploration in one context and updated the parser after discovering argparse edge behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material contrast is context transfer: parallel introduced lossy and incomplete child-facing context, while serial's single context preserved and extended the local findings.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a compact implementation with /output/lib/aes.mjs, /output/lib/pybytes.mjs, /output/lib/args.mjs, and /output/test16.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a different hierarchy with AES split under /output/aes and top-level args, pybytes, and test16 modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented AES and output formatting, but serial made a later parser rewrite while parallel kept the helper child's simpler parser.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All three parallel children completed and returned summaries; the parent consumed their file paths and at least read key helper modules before final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results and therefore no join boundary; it iterated locally through writes, probes, and final reporting.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had normal child completion and result reception, while serial had a local iterative lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote distinct files in /output and the entry child imported the agreed helper modules; no same-file or overwrite collision is visible.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial repeatedly rewrote its own files, including args.mjs, as one owner rather than through concurrent shared-state edits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared workspace writes were separated by file ownership and then integrated; serial used local rewrites with no cross-agent collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel relied on child-reported FIPS, formatting, parser, sample diff, missing-arg, and one extra random-case checks before the parent final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran sample diffs, argparse behavior probes, a rewritten parser check, and a larger combined suite with fuzzing before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification was broader around CLI parity, while parallel verification was distributed and left the helper brief's narrower parser scope in place.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 524 agent seconds, 25 LLM requests, and three subagents, then closed after reading modules and summarizing the solution.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 271 agent seconds, 12 LLM requests, no subagents, and closed after its broader local verification summary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more budget because of delegation and the AES vector investigation, but there was no timeout or child cancellation; both closed with failed official evaluation afterward.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records show both modes failed, each with 3/33 samples. The concrete process difference is not a pass/fail discordance: parallel relied on child delegation and inherited two coordination-quality problems, while serial kept implementation and verification local and explored more CLI edge cases. The raw trajectories do not expose the exact official hidden mismatches, so the retained labels are adverse parallel process patterns rather than proven causes of a different official result.
parallel_contributors: Parallel helper delegation narrowed the exact argparse parity requirement to a limited child brief.
Parallel AES delegation transferred an executable-derived sample as an incorrect hex expectation, causing avoidable child verification churn.
serial_contributors: Serial retained one owner for implementation and later rewrote parser behavior after observing argparse edge cases.
Serial still failed the official evaluator at the same 3/33 rate despite broader local checks.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two implementations used different file layouts and parser implementations.
Both relied on local sample and fuzz-style testing that did not reveal the hidden official failures.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns are adverse parallel process effects, not exclusive root causes

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership existed: AES, helper modules, and entry implementation were assigned and produced files.
The entry child owned consuming the helper contracts and integrating them into test16.mjs.
The entry-file child and then the parent had explicit responsibility for creating and presenting the deliverable tree.
The parent sequenced implementation, child results, integration, checks, and final delivery, so the end-to-end pipeline was not ownerless.
The initial executable probe was brief and did not block all productive work behind a mandatory serial gate with an unfinished-stage consequence.
The parallel run launched implementation children after a small probe rather than completing a separate all-investigation phase that starved implementation.
No indispensable path is shown as underallocated; the entry, helper, and AES work all completed and were joined.
Only two initial children and one later child ran; the run did not time out and no collective fan-out budget exhaustion is visible.
The AES and helper assignments completed and returned usable artifacts; no child was left unfinished because of overbroad scope.

The original prompt required exact CLI argument parity, but the helper child brief enumerated only a limited argparse subset and emphasized minimal scope, after which the parent accepted a reduced parser rather than the fuller behavior the serial run probed and implemented.
candidates.realized_consequence: The integrated parallel helper remained scoped to a subset of argparse behavior and was accepted without the broader CLI parity checks the serial run performed.
candidates.near_match_reason: The missing fact was an acceptance requirement for one child, not an interface contract between independently produced components.

candidates.reason: The parent supplied concrete module names and function signatures for AES, pybytes, args, and entry integration, and no inter-module incompatibility was observed.

The parent had already observed the executable's bytes repr for sample one, but the child-facing AES prompt converted the printable `a` byte into an `a1` hex byte; the child then spent multiple turns investigating a false mismatch and returned a typo warning.
candidates.realized_consequence: The AES child burned verification work on a non-real mismatch and returned a warning about a task-vector typo caused by the transferred value.
candidates.near_match_reason: The child was not reconciling two returned reports; the single handoff itself had lost byte-repr meaning during conversion.

No receiver acted on a handoff describing a superseded workspace state or stale requirement.
No incompatible completed child reports remained unadjudicated; the AES-vector problem was a lossy transfer into one child brief.
Although official evaluation later failed, the parent-visible trajectory did not contain a concrete unresolved integrated mismatch that the parent knowingly ignored before final response.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel helper child was not given the full exact argparse parity acceptance surface even though the parent prompt required exact command-line behavior; the child produced the narrower parser that the parent integrated.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The final parallel solution carried a simplified argument parser accepted from the child without the broader argparse parity pass visible in the serial control.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The module interfaces were named and compatible; the missing element was acceptance coverage in the child brief.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent transferred a known executable output into the AES child brief as an incorrect hex value, causing the child to chase a false mismatch and return a warning rather than simply consuming the sample as observed.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The AES child spent additional verification turns on a false pyaes-vector mismatch and propagated a typo warning into the parent handoff.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: There was no unresolved conflict between completed handoffs; the single transferred sample value was degraded before the child received it.
